signal: Current fund vintage and close date
why_it_matters: A fund in year one deploys. A fund in year six is managing reserves and will take the meeting without being able to act on it.
where_to_find: Search the management company on EDGAR for a recent Form D, then confirm against the firm's own announcement.
good_looks_like: Fund closed within the last two to three years.
bad_looks_like: No new vehicle in five or more years, or a close that was announced but never filed.

why_it_matters: Determines whether they can write the cheque at all, and whether they can follow on.
where_to_find: Fund size minus disclosed deployments, or a paid database estimate.
good_looks_like: Clear headroom relative to fund size and stated pace.
bad_looks_like: Late in the fund with most capital called.

signal: Typical first cheque at our stage
why_it_matters: Our ask has to sit inside their normal range or the conversation cannot converge.
where_to_find: Firm site, OpenVC, and the last several announced rounds at our stage.
good_looks_like: Our ask sits mid-range for them.
bad_looks_like: Our ask is below their minimum - we would be a rounding error and get no attention.

signal: Do they lead, or only follow?
why_it_matters: A round needs someone to price it. Filling a pipeline with followers produces a lot of meetings and no term sheet.
where_to_find: Recent announced rounds: were they named as lead?
good_looks_like: Led priced rounds at our stage in the last year.
bad_looks_like: Only ever participates; no pricing history.

signal: New investments announced in the last two quarters
why_it_matters: Distinguishes a firm that is deploying from one that is quietly paused.
where_to_find: Crunchbase or Dealroom deal feed, filtered by date.
good_looks_like: Steady cadence of new, not just follow-on, investments.
bad_looks_like: Only follow-ons, or nothing new for two quarters.

signal: Published thesis on applied AI in marketing or vertical AI
why_it_matters: Tells us whether we are explaining a category or joining a conversation they are already having.
where_to_find: Firm blog, published roadmaps, partner posts and podcast appearances.
good_looks_like: They have written about decisioning, agents or measurement.
bad_looks_like: No stated view; we would be doing the category education.

signal: Portfolio companies in martech, restaurant tech or CPG commerce
why_it_matters: Evidence they already understand the buyer, the budget and the sales cycle.
where_to_find: The firm's own portfolio page, checked company by company.
good_looks_like: Two or more genuinely adjacent companies.
bad_looks_like: Nothing in the category - every objection will be first-principles.

signal: Any investment in a company on our competitor watchlist
why_it_matters: We do not take meetings with funds that have backed a competitor. It leaks strategy and wastes the slot.
where_to_find: The firm's portfolio page against the competitor watchlist in this CRM.
bad_looks_like: A confirmed investment in a Blocking competitor - do not engage.

signal: Which specific partner would own this
why_it_matters: Firms do not invest; partners do. Without a named sponsor there is no process.
where_to_find: Signal by NFX, LinkedIn, and the partner's own writing and deal history.
good_looks_like: A named partner with matching deal history and a warm path to them.
bad_looks_like: No obvious owner, or the only fit is an associate.

why_it_matters: A departing partner strands their deals. A new partner is often hunting for a first cheque to prove out.
where_to_find: LinkedIn, the firm's team page, and the trade press.
good_looks_like: A newly promoted or newly joined partner building a book in our category.
bad_looks_like: Our likely sponsor has just left or moved to a part-time role.

signal: How decisions get made, and how long it takes
why_it_matters: Determines whether they can move inside our close window.
where_to_find: Ask them directly on the first call, and confirm with their founders.
good_looks_like: Small partnership, decision in weeks, clear steps.
bad_looks_like: Multi-stage committee, offshore IC, no stated timeline.

why_it_matters: Whether they can support the next round matters more than the first cheque.
where_to_find: Ask directly; confirm with portfolio founders.
good_looks_like: Explicit reserves and a track record of following on.
bad_looks_like: No reserves, or follow-on only for outliers.

signal: Board seat expectations and governance terms
why_it_matters: Shapes the terms conversation before it starts.
where_to_find: Ask directly; check their standard documents with counsel.
good_looks_like: Terms consistent with market for our stage.
bad_looks_like: Unusual control terms or a board seat at seed with a small cheque.

signal: Will they invest in a US-incorporated company with this founder base?
why_it_matters: Several India-based funds invest in US entities and several do not. This decides whether the whole conversation is possible.
where_to_find: The firm's own statements, plus their existing US-incorporated investments.
bad_looks_like: India-domiciled mandate only, or LP constraints preventing it.

signal: References from two of their founders they did not introduce
why_it_matters: How a firm behaves after the wire is the part no pitch reveals.
where_to_find: Find portfolio founders directly rather than accepting their reference list.
good_looks_like: Consistent, specific, unprompted positives - especially about a hard moment.
bad_looks_like: Hedged answers, or founders who will not take the call.

signal: LP base and any strategic constraints
why_it_matters: Strategic or corporate LPs can create information and conflict problems downstream.
where_to_find: Form ADV, press coverage, and direct questions.
good_looks_like: Institutional LP base with no strategic overlap.
bad_looks_like: Corporate LPs that compete with our customers or partners.

signal: Signals the firm is effectively out of the market
why_it_matters: Saves the highest-cost mistake: a full process with a fund that cannot invest.
where_to_find: Deal pace, partner departures, absence of a new fund, and trade press.
bad_looks_like: No new deals, partners leaving, no new fund, and evasive answers on timing.
